schema: cairn/lesson/v0.1
id: python-dulwich-unsanitized-commit-subject-filename
title: Commit subject used as filename component without sanitizing (path traversal in format-patch)
summary: A function derives a filename component from a commit message's first line and only replaces
  spaces with dashes. Characters such as `/`, `..`, backslashes or control characters stay in the name.
  A crafted commit subject can then make format-patch write outside the target directory or create odd
  filenames.
cwe:
- CWE-22
severity: high
confidence: medium
languages:
- python
source:
  kind: fix-commit
  ref: c2446e51b49e5bc0ad1b623e47f4b0b961ecaa46
  vulnerable_ref: c2446e51b49e5bc0ad1b623e47f4b0b961ecaa46^
  patched_ref: c2446e51b49e5bc0ad1b623e47f4b0b961ecaa46
  repository: https://github.com/jelmer/dulwich
rule:
  message: 'The first line of a commit message is turned into a filename-like string with only

    `.replace(" ", "-")`. Path separators, `..` and other special characters are not

    removed, which allows path traversal or filename injection. Sanitize with an

    allowlist (e.g. only [A-Za-z0-9._], other runs become "-") and limit the length.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern-either:
    - pattern: $LINES[0].replace(" ", "-")
    - pattern: $MSG.splitlines()[0].replace(" ", "-")
    - pattern: $MSG.split("\n")[0].replace(" ", "-")
  - pattern-not-inside: '_sanitize_subject_for_filename(...)

      '
fix:
  guidance: Do not build filenames from commit subjects by only swapping spaces. Pass the subject through
    a sanitizer like git's format_sanitized_subject, which keeps only [A-Za-z0-9._], collapses runs of
    other characters into a single "-", collapses repeated dots, truncates the result, and strips trailing
    "." and "-".
  example: "def get_summary(commit):\n    decoded = commit.message.decode(errors=\"replace\")\n    lines\
    \ = decoded.splitlines()\n    if not lines:\n        return \"\"\n    return _sanitize_subject_for_filename(lines[0])\n"
